Name: Sarah Almon
Badge: Teacher as Researcher: Cultivating Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

One of the things I realized is that I favor teaching with paper and pencil over technology in my classroom. Trying my hand at digital annotations for They Say/ I Say was a good learning experience for me, and I am glad that I went outside of my comfort zone for this. Additionally, I've talked with my students before about how reading should involve a conversation with the text. However, this can be difficult when annotations were done only between the student and a piece of paper. Doing this digitally allowed students to make comments and ask questions. Then, their peers were able to respond to the comments, which turned the experience into an actual conversation, which was fun to see taking place (even if it did get off topic a few times). Doing it this way helped my students get a better feel for what a conversation with a text can look like.
